Backup and recovery

The operator view of what CALIBER state must be preserved, what can be rebuilt, and where disaster recovery stops and asset-specific rollback begins.

OperatorRunbookGA
PrerequisitesA CALIBER deployment or disaster-recovery review
Reviewed 2026-10-14 · current main branch docs contract

Use this page when you need to know what CALIBER state must be preserved, how to copy each part, and where disaster recovery stops and asset-specific rollback begins.

Not rehearsed. The commands below are standard tools for each store and are correct as written, but the alpha has not run a full restore drill. Treat your first restore as a test, not a procedure, and rehearse it before you depend on it.

At a glance#

StateWhere it livesHoldsPreserve it?
CALIBER databaseCALIBER_DATABASE_URLprojects, members, accounts, jobs, approvals, release operations, the audit log, test sets, skills, workflows, knowledge-base metadatayes
MLflow backend storethe --backend-store-uri you gave mlflow serverprompt versions and their aliases, experiments, runs and tracesyes
MLflow artifact rootthe --default-artifact-root of your mlflow serverrun and trace artifactsyes
Object storethe S3 or MinIO buckets you use: any bucket you uploaded to, each knowledge base's source bucket, CALIBER_LOG_BUCKET and CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_ARTIFACT_BUCKET (CALIBER_OBJECT_STORE_* sets only the connection)uploads, knowledge-base sources and built indexes, log sink files, persisted run artifactsyes, if you use them
Workflow storageCALIBER_WORKFLOW_STORAGE_* (the bucket in CALIBER_WORKFLOW_STORAGE_BUCKET when the backend is s3)run workspaces, uploads and file-backed workflow evidenceyes, if you use workflows
Secret encryption keythe source named by CALIBER_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_SOURCEthe key that decrypts stored secretsyes, separately
Generated docs and UI assetsrepository build outputnothing uniqueno, rebuild

The row to notice is the MLflow backend store. Prompt versions and the prod alias live there, not in the CALIBER database. The CALIBER database holds the audit log and the release records that point at those versions. A backup of the CALIBER database alone restores a history that names versions the registry no longer has.

1. Back up the stores together#

Take the CALIBER database and the MLflow backend store at the same point in time, so releases recorded in one match the versions in the other. If they share one database or one SQLite file, one backup covers both.

PostgreSQL#

# CALIBER database
pg_dump --format=custom --file=caliber.dump "$CALIBER_DATABASE_URL"
# MLflow backend store: the same URI you passed to `mlflow server --backend-store-uri`
# (skip if it is the same database as above)
pg_dump --format=custom --file=mlflow.dump "$MLFLOW_BACKEND_STORE_URI"

Use a libpq URL (postgresql://user@host/db); replace the +psycopg driver suffix if your URL has one. Restore with pg_restore --clean --if-exists --dbname="$TARGET_URL" caliber.dump.

In the bundled Compose stack both stores are databases on the caliber-mcp-postgres container: caliber for CALIBER and mlflow for MLflow (its MLFLOW_BACKEND_URI). For example:

docker exec caliber-mcp-postgres pg_dump -U caliber --format=custom caliber > caliber.dump
docker exec caliber-mcp-postgres pg_dump -U caliber --format=custom mlflow > mlflow.dump

SQLite#

# Online, consistent copy; safe while the server runs
sqlite3 caliber.db ".backup 'caliber.backup.db'"
sqlite3 mlflow.db  ".backup 'mlflow.backup.db'"

Copying the file with cp while the server is writing can produce a torn copy. Use .backup, or stop the server first. Restore by putting the backup file back at the path in the URL.

Files and buckets#

# MLflow artifact root and workflow storage on local disk
rsync -a /path/to/mlflow-artifacts/ /backup/mlflow-artifacts/
rsync -a /path/to/workflow-storage/ /backup/workflow-storage/

# Object-store buckets (MinIO shown; use `aws s3 sync` for AWS S3). The bundled stack's
# buckets are `mlflow` (artifact root), `caliber-workspaces` (workflow storage) and `caliber-log`.
mc mirror --preserve local/caliber-workspaces /backup/caliber-workspaces

The secret encryption key#

Back up the key behind CALIBER_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_SOURCE somewhere other than the database backup. Without it, restored secrets cannot be decrypted.

2. Distinguish disaster recovery from feature rollback#

Restoring the deployment is not the same as rolling back a governed release. After a restore, use the product's own controls: roll a prompt back from its version history, or use the recovery console on the Releases page for a release that was left incomplete.

3. After a restore#

Run caliber-migrate against the restored CALIBER database so its schema matches the installed release (the bundled CALIBER container runs alembic upgrade head each time it starts), then verify:

  • GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/readiness reports ready: true, including the schema check
  • the version history of a prompt you know (Prompts, then its Author stage) shows the versions and the live badge you expect
  • the Releases page lists what was live, and the Audit Log shows the history
  • on the Releases page, Reconcile releases reports nothing incomplete. A release that was in flight when the backup was taken can be left applying or prepared, and the console resolves it against the registry.
